Section85A imposes an obligation on the revenue court to refer any issue arising under the provisions of the Tenancy Acts and if section 85 A imposes an obligations on the Revenue Court to decide, decide or dealtwith by the appropriate authorities under that Act, it shall be referred for the competent Authority under the Mamlatdar Act. The jurisdiction of civil courts to settle is ousted because, the issue arises within a properly formed civil suit triable by the civil Courts having jurisdiction to entertain and deal in the same. [540C] 5. Section 86A imposes a duty on the Mamlatdar to refer the issue arising to the Civil Tribunal under the Indian Tenancy Act. If section 85 provides for an additional issue arising out of a properly appointed civil suit, the Court has no jurisdiction under the said Act to decide the same and upon the reference being answered back, to dispose of the suit in accordance with the decision of the competent court under the Civil Law.

The assessee company was carrying on the business of heavy engineering. The assessee company had been carrying on its business in the manufacture and sale of Jute Mill Division, Calcutta. The two industrial undertakings were formed by reconstruction of the business already existing and hence they were not formed by the reconstruction of their business already in existence. The Income tax Officer held that the Steel Foundry Division was an industrial undertaking to which section 15C of the Indian Income Tax Act, 1922 applied ? The Appellate Assistant Commissioner on the above facts held that since the articles produced by the two undertakings are used by the Boiler Division of the assessee 's business already there can be no controversy. On appeal by the Revenue, the High Court held that these two industrial companies were formed in reconstruction of its business already and hence the assessee was not entitled to exemption under section 15 C(2) as rightly so held by the High court since they were formed on reconstruction of a new industrial undertaking which had been the end product of the assesse ding 's main business. Allowing the appeals, ^ HELD: 1. The High Court was right in answering the two questions in the negative and against the assessee. [776D] 2.1 In order that the new industrial undertakings of the assesses should not be formed out of the already existing business, there must be a new emergence of a physically separate industrial unit which may exist on its own as a viable unit. The fact that an assessee by establishment of a fresh industrial undertaking expands his existing business which he certainly does would not prevent him from setting up new industrial company and from claiming benefit under section15C if that section is otherwise applicable. [771E] 2:2 In order to be entitled to the benefit under s 15C, the following facts have to be established by the assessee : (i) establishment of new industrial unit expands its existing business; (ii) employment of requisite labour therein, (iii) manufacture or production of articles in the said undertaking, (iv) earning of profits clearly attributa ble to the said new undertaking, and (v) above all, a separate and distinct identity of the industrial unit set up. [761G] 2 :3 The fact of the existence of which there can been no controversy, as found by the Tribunal, cannot be held to. be decisive to deny the benefit of section 15B merely because it goes to expand the general business of the appellant on some directions. The facts that the assessee is carrying on a particular business to set up a new Industrial Unit on account of which exemption of tax under section 10C may be claimed. [751E F] 2(i) The fact, that an assesse sion by establishmentof a new manufacturing unit expand s his existing industrial undertaking, which he undoubtedly does, would not affect the benefit conferred under section 14C. [773G H] 3:2 The fact in the instant case that the articles manufactured by the three undertakings are utilised by the boiler Division of a assessee will not prevent them from settingup new industrial units and from claim claiming benefit u/s 15C if this section is not otherwise applicable, [774A B] 4.1 The fact whether an assessee has carried on a business to carry on a specific business to setting up a fresh Industrial Unit, which may be of aid to the principal business but yet the undertaking are distinct and not reconstruction out of existing business of that assessee. The mere fact that the article produced by two undertakings is used by a Boiler Division will not affect his benefit under Section 15C merely because he goes to expanded the general trade of the assessees on some direction.

The inamdars were granted to the temple for the performance of services connected therewith. They were allowed to continue as tenants under the inamdars and were paid remuneration for services to be rendered by them and were within the purview of section 44 B(2)(a) (i). The inamdars filed suits in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Madurai against the Government and the State of Madras. The suit was withdrawn to the Court. The District Judge held that the inam lands were personal inams burdened with services and the order of resumption was therefore illegal and a nullity. In appeal to this Court it was contended on behalf of the appellants (i) that the grant from the inamdar was not within the ambit of section44 B(1)(a)(i). Held, that the right of resumption could be so extinguished by adverse possession, and (ii) that there was no alienation of the inams as contemplated by section 44B(2) (a) and (5) the right to resume an inam land was extinguished by a adverse possession. The grant from inamdar to any subordinate interest in the inams was not adverse to the Government under whom the inamdaridars held the inam land. The inamdar could acquire prescriptive title to the kudiwaram rights against the State and thereby defeat the latter 's right to resumption the inam does not, therefore, arise for decision. It may be noted that in Roman Catholic Mission vs State of Bombay, (1955) 1 S.C.R. 869), this Court held that there is no limitation barring imposition of assessment on the land after resuming the melwaram.

The appellant Corporation was governed by the Indore City Municipal Act, 1909. The Indore Municipality however purported to levy the house tax on buildings at the rate of 7% of such value for the financial years 1953 54 and 1954 55. The Municipality however purporting to levy tax on the basis of the gross annual letting value less 10% statutory allowance in lieu of costs of repairs or on any other account whatsoever. The Municipal tax levied under the old Act and the rules framed thereunder on the ground that under the 1954 Act the tax could be assessed on the net and not the gross income less 10%. The Municipality contended that under section 79(1) of the 1954 act the Corporation was entitled to levy house tax at the rates of 7%, but it was not bound to deduct the 10% allowance provided by sec. 2(c). Held, that the Municipal tax is an annual tax leviable for a particular official year and the assessment list on the assumption that the valuation or the annual letting values are conclusive evidence for purposes of all municipal taxes of the valuationor annual letting Value of buildings is for each such official year. The Corporation was not entitled to demand the tax assessed on its gross annual rent at the same rate as it was inconsistent with sec. 73 of the Act. The appellant Corporation had no right to demand tax assessed under the new Act and that the tax imposed under the 1955 Act and rules framed therein on the strength of which the list for 1952 53 was prepared was in force during the years in question and had to be accepted under section 76(6) as conclusive evidence of the annual rent.

The assessee Company was incorporated in 1937 primarily with the object of acquiring and working the rights, title and interest in a match factory belonging to one A. V. The Deputy Commissioner, however, relying on the Memorandum of Association, which allowed the assessee Company to manufacture and sell chemicals and raw materials and obtained a larger price, held that the transaction was not during the carrying on of the business or even for the purpose of carrying on the business, but had the characteristics of a trading sale. The Tribunal found that the business had not been completely discontinued, since the assessee company was carrying on manufacturing, on behalf of the purchaser and, the sale could not be regarded as a realisation sale after the Company was wound up. On appeal by the Commissioner of Income Tax, Kerala, the High Court held that there was no profit other than what results from the appreciation of capital. The Revenue appealed to this Court. HELD : (i) There is no doubt in this case that the assessee was woundup at least in so far as its match manufacturing business was concerned. That the business of the Company had been sold as a going concern, and was, in fact worked by the assessee on behalf Of the buyer till the entire consideration was paid, makes no difference because the agreement clearly indicated that the appellant Company was keeping the factory going not on its own behalf but entirely on behalf and the price with them. [357 F G] (ii) The sales were not part of the realisation of the trading stock and winding up of the businesses, which alone would have attracted tax if profit resulting from a trade or business operation was attributable to a trade. [457 E] (iii) There was no evidence in this connection that the chemicals and the raw materials were sold in the ordinary way of business or that the price without the chemicals, and raw material was paid. The assessee Company had not sold any chemical or raw materials except by comparing the two prices offered to be paid by the buyer, that is to say, the price after the chemicals were sold, made no difference, because the transaction clearly indicated the price at without the chemical and raw goods and the cost with them, and that the balance of a slump price which was paid was, therefore, inferentially attributable to the stock. [557 F] (iv) The assessee company had not purchased any chemical nor raw materials excepting by comparing it two prices offer to be made by the buyers, that was to say the price on behalf, that being, to say that the value without the Chemical and raw articles and the sale price with those chemicals and other raw materials was paid there makes no distinction. [657 F H] (v) The transaction was a winding up sale with a view to realising the capital assets of the assessee 973 Company and not a sale in the course of business operations, which itself would have attract tax.
